A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same LDMol research. Their complete text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–B support reliable comparison despite substantial reformatting and added material in v3.

before.justification: v2 reports original molecule-generation, retrieval, editing, and ablation results in Tables 1–3 and the main-text and appendix figures.

after.justification: v3 retains those original experiments and adds generation benchmarks, latent-space analyses, prompt evaluations, additional ablations, and computational-efficiency results.

M1.justification: The contrastive SMILES encoder, stereoisomer hard negatives, linear compression, autoregressive decoder, text-conditioned DiT, and downstream algorithms are retained. Newly documented architectural details and alternative compression experiments do not establish a change to the proposed LDMol procedure.

E1.justification: Table 1 adds text-to-molecule generation evaluation on PCDes, previously used for training and retrieval. Figure 11 adds ambiguous and contradictory input scenarios. The existing training datasets, ChEBI-20 generation, retrieval tasks, and editing coverage remain.

E2.justification: Table 6 adds MolT5large and bioT5+ comparisons to the previously LDMol-only handwritten-prompt studies; Table 8 also compares their computational costs. Comparator membership in the retained ChEBI-20 and retrieval benchmarks is unchanged.

E3.justification: v3 substantially expands evaluation through uniqueness, novelty, substructure-based alignment, and V×U×A metrics for the 1,000-sample prompt studies. New analyses introduce temperature and latent-width controls, reconstruction testing on 1,000 unseen SMILES, and scaffold-group UMAP sampling. Existing generation and retrieval settings remain intact.

E4.justification: Appendices A.2 and B add temperature, compression-width, training-placement, and transformer-compression ablations; scaffold visualizations; quantitative prompt analyses; ambiguous/contradictory-input tests; and efficiency analysis. Earlier compression and stereoisomer ablations are retained in Table 7. The brief random-versus-fixed initialization comparison in v2 is omitted.

E5.justification: Editing results retain error bars and the description of means and standard deviations over three runs, moved from v2's Figure 5 caption to v3's Appendix A.3. No new seed disclosure, confidence intervals, significance tests, or repeated-run reporting practice is introduced.

E6.justification: v3 newly reports PCDes generation results, including LDMol's 0.464 exact match and 0.32 FCD. Tables 5–8 add reconstruction, prompt-quality, compression-ablation, and runtime/memory outcomes. Original ChEBI-20 and retrieval scores remain identical; v2's qualitative finding of marginal sensitivity to random versus zero-vector initialization is removed.

T1.justification: The diffusion equations, contrastive and reconstruction losses, and Algorithms 1–2 retain the same mathematics, apart from notation corrections. Added mechanism explanations and empirical metric descriptions introduce no substantive formal assumptions, proofs, or derivations.

C1.justification: The introduction now calls a latent domain essential for effective diffusion on complex molecule-generation tasks, strengthening v2's beneficial-design framing. AR superiority and applications without task-specific training were already claimed in v2; their increased prominence in the title and abstract does not establish new contributions.

C2.justification: v3 adds explanations connecting temperature to hard-negative sensitivity and complex compression to disruption of informative features. It discusses the reconstruction–cost tradeoff behind latent width 64, identifies very long molecules among reconstruction failures, and describes boundaries under ambiguous or contradictory prompts. The biological-property limitation remains.

D1.justification: v3 supplies a training/sampling code-access link, specifies 12-layer BERT-based encoder/decoder implementations, reports eight 40-GB A100 GPUs, and discloses 320,000 diffusion-training examples. These supplement existing implementation information; they do not establish changed training data or default hyperparameters.

R1.justification: Background coverage expands to discrete and embedding-based text diffusion and molecular LLMs, including Austin et al., Li et al., and DrugLLM. New analyses add supporting citations. InfoNCE attribution changes from Chen et al. to Oord et al.; the central positioning around structurally informative latent diffusion remains.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, motivation, and background receive localized rewrites. Hard-negative details move into implementation, detailed ablations move into Appendix B.6, and acknowledgments and an impact statement are added. The overall section sequence and much of the existing exposition remain.

P2.justification: The single-column preprint becomes a predominantly two-column conference paper. Figure 1 is redrawn, Figure 4 panels are rearranged, editing examples move from Figure 5 to Figure 12, and the original ablation table is split. New plots and tables substantially expand the visual presentation.

improvement.justification: v2 supported broad-prompt generation largely through examples and validity. v3 adds quantitative diversity and alignment comparisons, novelty measurements, and explicit failure cases, substantially strengthening and qualifying that evidence. Additional PCDes evaluation, latent-space/design analyses, and implementation disclosures further improve validation and reproducibility. The stronger necessity claim and underspecified timing comparison remain weaknesses, but the overall evidential gains are substantial.
